messages:
amelia: Heads-up — kicked off a targeted burn-in on node g2-33 (rack usw2-rack7) after 3 intermittent Xid 79 events last week. Trying a hybrid soak to surface the flake. I dumped the last kernel dmesg and attached below.

sam: thanks. what's the exact recipe? previous runs were either pure mem-stress or long thermal cycles; we may need both + a synthetic inference workload.

amelia: Agreed. Plan: 24h combined run:
- 8h thermal-cycle (fans + power variations)
- 12h mem-transfer-heavy workload (p2p memcpy, large batch size)
- continuous small-chat synthetic traffic to keep KV cache active
- enable ECC scrubbing logs and nv_peer_mem on the host

Running with our new isolated pool so it doesn't affect production scheduling. Command I'm using: 
```bash
./soak-repro --node g2-33 --cycles 6 --mem-stress 90 --threads 64 --workload chat-sim --log /var/log/soak/g2-33.log
```

observed Xid snippet from dmesg: 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 79, PID=2314, GPU=0000:af:00.0, channel=2
[ 12345.678962] NVRM: GPU 0000:af:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

sam: nice. can we also toggle ECC scrubbing frequency during the run? might provoke an ECC-induced failure.

amelia: yes, toggled via sysfs before the run. also increased driver log level temporarily.

vikram: if this reproduces, what's the gate for returning to service? e.g., 48h clean run or N cycles w/o Xids?

amelia: proposal: 48h without new Xids + stable thermals (<5°C delta) + successful CUDA smoke tests (nvcc kernels) x3. If fail -> mark as RMA candidate and isolate.

ryan: region capacity: we only have 2 spare replacement GPUs in us-west-2 stock. If g2-33 needs RMA, we might have to evict capacity to keep SLA for dedicated pools. cost impact for swapping racks mid-commit will be ~1.2x for the month. FYI.

julia: can we shift some low-priority Dedicated batches to our burst pool in us-east-1 for 24-48h instead of immediate replacement? avoids emergency RMA and buys time to repro.

amelia: yes, scheduler policy change looks safe for short term. I'm labeling the node with `quarantine:soak` so autoscaler won't schedule prod jobs.

ops-bot: Node g2-33 labeled quarantine:soak by amelia. Isolation pool set: isolated-burnin-usw2.

quarantine-bot: Node g2-33 quarantined — no external traffic allowed. Logs forwarded to /mnt/soak-archive/g2-33/2032104567.tar.gz

sam: small ask — can we add a periodic PCIe rescan + soft reset step in the recipe? We saw temporary bus-drop recoveries before. Something like `echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/rescan` between cycles.

amelia: added. Also running a low-level memory hammering pass (memtester-style) between cycles to stress ECC.

vikram: can you drop the soak script into the infra repo? want to run the same on other flaky nodes (g2-41, g2-52) if this surfaces the issue.

amelia: pushed a draft to infra/soak-recipes (PR 482). Test run link: https://soakboard.internal/runs/2032104567

sre-oncall: Thanks — I'll monitor alerts. If Xid spikes >2 in 1h we'll escalate and start a replacement ticket.

ryan: note for cost planning — if we start parallel reproductions in multiple racks we'll need approval from finance because it eats into spare budget for the month. pinged finance.

julia: ack. If repro fails after two full hybrid runs, what's the fallback? do we re-image and rotate driver/kernel versions?

amelia: fallback plan: 1) reimage host (stock kernel + clean driver), 2) rerun hybrid soak once, 3) if still flaky -> RMA. Documented in the PR.

sam: perfect. keep logs minimal and tag `soak:hybrid-v1`. small messages preferred in thread. :thumbsup:

amelia: will do. I'll post final pass + verdict in this thread when the run completes (expected in ~26h).

sre-oncall: I'll watch cloudwatch, set a watch for `Xid>=1` on that node and route alerts to #incidents if triggered.

ryan: thanks all — good coordination.
